features.feature_value: They judged the pair by whether both comments would contribute constructively to the conversation/topic.
features.evidence_span: evaluated whether or not both of the comments as a pair would contribute constructively
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes assessing the pair’s combined constructive value.

features.feature_value: They mostly used whether posts invited discussion vs were mainly insults/negative content.
features.evidence_span: invited discussion or if they were just insults or negative content
features.rationale: They state a primary rule comparing discussion potential to insult/negativity.

features.feature_value: They screened for inciting violence and otherwise treated them as acceptable if comparable to benign cheering/fan behavior.
features.rationale: The reflection centers on whether posts incited violence as the key removal criterion.

features.feature_value: They preferred removing content that was aggressively rude/hurtful because it added little to the subject; yet they still support free speech in principle.
features.evidence_span: Anything too aggressively rude with logic I wanted removed because it did little to contribute
features.rationale: They link removal to hurtful rudeness not contributing, while also noting a countervailing free-speech belief.

features.feature_value: They distinguished between genuine discussable content and obvious rage-bait.
features.evidence_span: actualty something people could discuss vs obvious rage bait
features.rationale: The participant’s decision is framed around detectability of rage-bait versus real discussion value.

features.feature_value: They checked for radical/misinformation indicators and otherwise treated it as acceptable criticism.
features.evidence_span: radical information that indicated misinformation and was simply criticism that it was deemed ok
features.rationale: They describe misinformation/radicality as a disqualifier, with criticism treated as acceptable.

features.feature_value: They sometimes decided that only one of the two should be removed rather than removing both.
features.evidence_span: not both should be removed but one
features.rationale: They explicitly indicate a selective approach to which member of the pair to remove.

features.feature_value: They perceived ideological alignment (left/right) and felt both should not be used when cursing/out-of-line content occurred.
features.evidence_span: posts reflected very closely along the lines of what someone leaning left or right would say
features.rationale: They mention both ideological mirroring and a threshold triggered by cursing/out-of-line behavior.
